newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand approves plan to expand Don Muang airport.
newsitem.headline: Thailand approves plan to expand Don Muang airport.

text.p: Thailand's Board of Airport Development on Friday agreed to a proposal to expand Bangkok's international airport and postponed a decision on suspended plans for a 100 billion baht ($3.85 billion) second airport.
The government board was originally expected to make a decision on the fate of the planned second international airport at Nong Ngu Hao in Bangkok's eastern outskirts.
Earlier this month the government decided to suspend the second airport project and instead concentrate on expanding the existing Don Muang International Airport, just north of Bangkok.

"Since the Nong Ngu Hao project will not be completed on schedule the board committee chaired by the prime minister (Chavalit Yongchaiyudh) agreed to expand Don Muang airport instead to handle passengers for the next 10 years," Suvat Liptapanlop, minister of transport and communications, said after the meeting.

He said the current airport could be expanded to handle up to 40 million passengers per year following an offer by the Air Force to give up land adjacent to Don Muang for the expansion. The airport currently has a maximum capacity of 31 million passengers annually.
Don Muang aiport is in the compound of the headquarters of the Royal Thai Air Force.
Suwat said since the expanded Don Muang airport would be able to meet growing passenger needs through the year 2010, the committee decided to continue studying the Nong Ngu Hao project.

"The committee will study the pros and cons of the Nong Ngu Hao project and will report to the government later this month, but I would like to stress that Nong Ngu Hao is to continue but we have to study how to adjust the project," he said.
The Nong Ngu Hao project was initiated in 1960 but due to indecision by different governments, little progress has been made. It was originally due to open in 2000.
The government has said it decided to suspend the construction of the second airport in the interests of fiscal discipline.

The first phase of construction was about to begin when the suspension was announced. The government has vowed to negotiate with companies involved on meeting its obligations to them. It said it was committed to honouring the 18 contracts it has signed with companies at a total value of 18 billion baht. ($1 = 26 baht)
